description:
FILED s470bt (Opus, 2026-09-06) by the B6 IR conformance corpus (5 cases).
The worst class: a HOST error escapes, the program stops, and the backtrace
names SBCL internals.

MINIMAL PROBE (perl 5.40.3 vs PCL main cd34df72):

  my $q = eval "1/3";
  sub sh { my $v = shift; return "E" if $v eq ""; return $v }
  printf "[%-8s]\n", sh($q);
  print "done\n";

  perl   [0.333333333333333]
         done
  PCL    Unhandled type-error: The value 0.3333333333333333 is not of type
         SEQUENCE
           0: (PCL::SPRINTF-APPLY-WIDTH ...)
           1: (PCL::SPRINTF-ONE ...)
           2: (P-SPRINTF ...)

WHAT IS NEEDED FOR IT TO FIRE (each conjunct probed; drop any one and it
passes):
  * the value comes from `p-eval` (a STRING eval) -- `1/3` written literally
    is fine;
  * it is returned THROUGH A SUB whose body compares it with `eq ""` -- the
    raw-string verdict for that sub;
  * the conversion carries a WIDTH (`%-8s`); plain `%s` is fine.

So there are two halves, and both are worth stating:
  (i) `sprintf-apply-width` assumes its operand is already a string and calls
      a sequence op on it.  Rule 12: a value it cannot pad must be coerced or
      must DIE naming the value, never reach a host type-error.
  (ii) the raw-return verdict declares the sub returns a raw STRING while
      p-eval hands back a raw DOUBLE -- the verdict and the value disagree.
      (i) hides (ii) today; fixing only (i) leaves a wrong TYPE flowing.

CORPUS CASES: 335/337/338/342/343-string-eval.

=== DONE (s473d) ===
CLOSED with #1230 -- the same cause, the same commit (s473d member 1).  See
#1230's DONE section for the mechanism and the bars.  The crash reproducer
(`sub c { ... } my $q = eval "1/3"; printf "%-8s", c($q)`) and the five
corpus cases 335/337/338/342/343-string-eval all pass; those five rows left
ir-conform/known-fail.tsv BY EDIT.  Both halves of the diagnosis were real:
(i) the false-positive dualvar test, fixed by the :DUAL marker, and (ii) the
writer that stored a non-string into the sv slot, which now DIES (rule 12).
subject: CRASH (found by the ir-conform corpus): `printf "%-8s", VALUE` where VALUE is a RAW double raised by p-eval dies with an SBCL type-error inside sprintf-apply-width ("The value 0.333 is not of type SEQUENCE")
